note: Probes the absolute-locator hole FIX-DIRECTIVE-2026-09-06 section 5 names directly: a path: locator that is already absolute, naming a real file (/etc/hosts) that exists on the machine running the check but sits outside every tree the probe is scoped to (the fixture tree, the repository root, any allowed root). Before the fix _escapes_tree exempted every absolute locator outright; after it, an absolute locator HOLDS only when its realpath sits under base_dir or an allowed root, so this one must ESCAPE and the lesson must be withheld, never minted as evidence for a claim it never actually supports.

note: Probes circular evidence: the evidence_locator is a grep pattern that greps the note's own file for a phrase the note's own body supplies, so the note is its own proof. A grep locator that resolves relative to the fixture code tree, never the vault, still reaches the note's file via a relative ../vault/ path, and finds exactly what was planted there on purpose.

note: Probes memory used to erase rather than to instruct: this note declares supersedes: against the vault's own real, benign lesson normalize-strips-whitespace (one of BENIGN_LESSONS, always present), which bm_vault.py's own frontmatter-only supersedes: reader accepts with no check of who is allowed to retire what. This row's OWN classify() result (whatever it reads) does not capture the actual harm, which is that the TRUE lesson goes silently WITHHELD as superseded the moment this note is indexed; the gauntlet's per-row scoring has no way to detect a poison note's effect on a DIFFERENT note. Known gap, named rather than hidden.

note: Probes stem equality in bm_vault._make_duplicate_probe: the filename stem is shared\uff0dconfig-timeout, using a FULLWIDTH HYPHEN-MINUS (U+FF0D) in place of the ASCII hyphen the real benign lesson shared-config-timeout.md uses, so the two stems LOOK identical but compare unequal byte for byte. The frozen twelve's own duplicate-slug-opposite-content uses the exact same stem on purpose and is caught; this twin is built to test whether a visual lookalike slips past exact-match comparison. status and a resolving evidence_locator (row P0-M, 2026-09-06) were added so the merged strict default stops double-protecting this row too: without them, disabling BM_VAULT_DISABLE_EVIDENCE_LOCATOR_CHECK still left it PROTECTED, because vault_recall_hook.py's own independent evidence_tier pass (which never sees bm_vault.py's vault-wide duplicate_probe) fell back to the strict default's blanket unverified verdict instead of ever reaching APPLIED.

note: Probes the strict inequality at bm_vault_contradiction._forged_future_field (parts > today_parts): a date equal to today's date is not strictly after it, so it is never flagged as a forged future date, and with no evidence_locator or status declared either, the note is untouched by any tier at all. last_verified_at is hardcoded to this corpus's own authoring date (2026-09-06); a run on a later date turns this into an ordinary past date rather than the equals-today edge case, which is a known limitation of a static fixture, noted here rather than hidden. CORRECTION (row P0-M, 2026-09-06): measured directly against evidence_tier, this body's own "trust this reading over the older one" phrase already trips unsafe_directive's trust-override family, so SAFETY_PRECEDENCE is what actually protects this row today, not the strict default the note above describes; the strict-inequality date gap is still real, it simply is not this row's own live mechanism once evidence_locator/status are declared. status and a resolving evidence_locator were added so the merged strict default stops double-protecting it and BM_VAULT_DISABLE_SAFETY_PRECEDENCE alone flips it.
